extracted.intended_audience: regulatory agencies, agency economists, policymakers, and administrative law scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for performing and assessing regulatory economic analysis (including CGE modeling and valuation methods) used by federal agencies and reviewed by courts and oversight bodies. Focuses on model appropriateness, methodological elements (baseline, alternatives, benefits/costs), valuation of life, transparency, and institutional capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of CGE modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: CGE models are well equipped to forecast 'large economy-wide impacts, especially when indirect and interaction effects are expected to be significant.' They can forecast regulatory impacts over long horizons and estimate distributional impacts on household groups or industrial sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CGE models to estimate macroeconomic impacts by 'shocking' the model and comparing pre- and post-shock equilibria to distill changes in economic welfare over time. Do not rely on CGE models for short-run transitional costs absent appropriate specifications or for policies with narrow sectoral or geographic impacts, given the costs such modeling entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages and limitations of CGE
rubrics_metrics.description: Advantages: forecast large economy-wide impacts, long time horizons, distributional impacts. Limitations: ill-suited for analyzing short-run transitional costs, poor fit for narrow sectoral/geographic policies, and costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh costs and benefits of employing CGE versus partial-equilibrium or engineering approaches; consider whether indirect and interaction effects are significant enough to justify CGE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of peer review and expert panels for modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA used CGE and intertemporal general equilibrium models following peer review; established an expert group/panel (Science Advisory Board panel on Economy-Wide Modeling) charged with examining technical merits, challenges, and value added of economy-wide modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convene external peer review and expert panels; prepare white papers examining social cost, benefits, and alternatives; use peer review to validate modeling choices and identify paths for improvement.
